name: Song Yiquan

name: Bithal Das Mundhra
current_role: Chairman Emeritus, Simplex Infrastructures Ltd (Kolkata); formerly Chairman & Managing Director
profile: Patriarch of the Kolkata Mundhra family, which bought Simplex (a British-owned piling firm founded in 1924) in 1947 and grew it into a large Indian EPC/infrastructure contractor. He ran it as Chairman & MD. Simplex is now led by the next generation (Rajiv and Amitabh Mundhra), and he holds the title of Chairman Emeritus.
interesting_fact: Simplex started in 1924 as a British-owned piling company. The Mundhra family acquired it in 1947, listed it in 1996 as Simplex Concrete Piles (India), and renamed it Simplex Infrastructures in 2005.
deep_cut_fact: Born in 1942, he began his construction career at 19 on Simplex's construction sites before rising to lead the company.
notes: Born 1942; no recent public activity found, so his status is unconfirmed. The email is Simplex's general registered-office (Kolkata) address, not a personal one. The NBMCW source page now returns 404 (fact seen in a search snippet). One 2010 quote credits Simplex's growth to 'honest hard work, a progressive attitude and adaptability'.

name: Christopher E Kubasik
current_role: Former Chair & CEO, L3Harris Technologies (removed Aug 2026); no new role announced
profile: CPA and former Ernst & Young partner who became CFO and then President/COO of Lockheed Martin. He joined L3 Technologies in 2015 and became CEO in 2017. He led the 2019 L3-Harris merger and was CEO of L3Harris from 2021 (Chair from 2022). His wealth comes from L3Harris equity. In Aug 2026 the board terminated him after a code-of-conduct investigation, and Sam Mehta succeeded him.
interesting_fact: He went from Ernst & Young partner to Lockheed Martin controller in 1999, then CFO in 2004 and President/COO in 2010. He also completed the Defense Acquisition University's Systems Acquisition Management course for flag officers (2004).
deep_cut_fact: University of Maryland Athletics runs a career-readiness program for student-athletes named for him, the 'Kubasik First Impact Program'. He is a 1983 magna cum laude accounting graduate of UMD's Smith School.
notes: SENSITIVE: L3Harris fired him on 16-17 Aug 2026 over conduct (https://fortune.com/2026/08/17/l3harris-ceo-ousted-chris-kubasik-sam-mehta/). In 2012 he also left Lockheed as CEO-elect over an ethics issue. The L3Harris press email no longer reaches him. No personal channel was found. Approach with care or deprioritise.

name: Darren M Rebelez
current_role: Chairman, President & CEO, Casey's General Stores (CASY)
profile: West Point graduate and former Army Ranger who built a career in fuel and convenience retail. He spent time at ExxonMobil and Thornton Oil, was COO of 7-Eleven, and served as president of IHOP. He became Casey's CEO in 2019 and Chair in 2023. Casey's is the third-largest US convenience-store chain and is known for its pizza, and it joined the S&P 500 in 2026.
interesting_fact: Before his civilian career he was an Army Ranger and Gulf War veteran. He is a San Diego native and earned a BS in Foreign Area Studies at West Point.
deep_cut_fact: Before oil and c-stores, his early civilian jobs were at Fuddruckers and PepsiCo. He told CSP Daily he spent his whole post-military career 'either in the restaurant business or the' convenience business.

public_contacts.value: Casey's media relations: Katie Petru, (515) 446-6772 (company line)
Casey's investor relations: Sam James, (515) 446-6506 (company line, Aug 2026 release)

notes: Casey's press releases list phone contacts but no email. Energy angle: Casey's is a large fuel retailer, roughly 2,900 stores across the Midwest/South.

name: Nicholas Little
current_role: Senior Vice President & Chief Operating Officer, DXP Enterprises (DXPE), Houston
profile: Nick Little is a long-time DXP Enterprises operator. DXP is a Houston-based distributor of pumps, rotating equipment, MRO and safety products, with large exposure to oil & gas and industrial customers. He rose from application engineer through outside sales, director of operations and regional VP of sales & operations, and became COO effective January 2022. His wealth is mainly DXP stock.
interesting_fact: Leadership changed in January 2022. Nick Little and Paz Maestas were appointed COO and Chief Marketing & Technology Officer together as part of DXP's next-generation management team.
deep_cut_fact: His career at DXP began about 18 years before his 2022 COO promotion, as an application engineer, a technical pump/equipment role, before he moved into outside sales.
notes: Low public profile. An aggregator says he is the son of DXP CEO David R. Little, but no primary filing confirming this was found, so don't rely on it. DXP serves the energy, water and industrial pump markets, which is a relevant podcast angle. No DXP press or IR email was found. A Baylor BBA (Finance) is reported only by aggregators and is unverified.

name: Sanjay Chandrakant Kirloskar
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, Kirloskar Brothers Ltd (Pune)
profile: Born 1957 in Nagpur. He is a fourth-generation member of the Kirloskar industrial family and has led Kirloskar Brothers, India's largest pump maker, for decades. He took it global with acquisitions including SPP Pumps (UK, 2002), Braybar (South Africa), SyncroFlo (USA, 2014) and Rodelta (Netherlands, 2015). He studied mechanical engineering at Illinois Institute of Technology (1978).
interesting_fact: Under him, Kirloskar Brothers received the ASME N-Stamp in 2012. It was the first Indian rotating-equipment company to do so, which qualified it to make pumps for nuclear power plants.
deep_cut_fact: He set up KBL's all-women-run pump plant at Kaniyur near Coimbatore (c. 2010-11) to give rural women engineering jobs. Its team entered the Limca Book of Records by assembling a pump in 17.25 seconds.
notes: Energy/water angle: pumps for power plants, including nuclear, and irrigation. A 2025 interview at theworldfolio.com/interviews/engineering-leader-a/3889/ explains why he started the women's plant. Avoid the long-running Kirloskar family trademark dispute. The emails come from listing aggregators that cite exchange filings; check the latest BSE/NSE filing to confirm them.

name: Pooja Singhal
current_role: Promoter-group member / trustee (Alpha and Beta family trusts), PI Industries
profile: Pooja Singhal is in the promoter group of PI Industries, the Gurugram-based agrochemical and custom-synthesis company built by the Singhal family (founder P.P. Singhal; Salil Singhal, Chairman Emeritus; Mayank Singhal, Vice Chairman & MD). PI's filings list her as a trustee of family trusts that each hold about 4% of PI. She has no operating role and no public profile was found.
interesting_fact: PI Industries is one of India's leading agrochemical and contract-chemistry (CSM) companies. It makes active ingredients for global crop-protection majors.
notes: Private family shareholder. She appears only in shareholding filings, not in management. Her exact relation to the operating Singhals is not established in sources, so it is not stated. If contact is wanted, the best route is through PI Industries' corporate office.

name: Gregory A Heckman
current_role: Chief Executive Officer, Bunge Global SA (BG), St. Louis
profile: Agribusiness and energy trader who has been CEO of Bunge since 2019 (board since 2018). He led its merger with Viterra and took it into the S&P 500 in 2023. Earlier he was CEO of The Gavilon Group (2008-15), where he grew its agriculture and energy arms before selling them to Marubeni and NGL Energy Partners. Before that he held COO roles at ConAgra.
interesting_fact: Bunge sits at the centre of renewable-fuel feedstocks such as soy oil for renewable diesel. Heckman also serves on the board of the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis and is a non-executive director of fertilizer maker OCI NV.
deep_cut_fact: Before Bunge he was a founding partner of Flatwater Partners. He holds a B.S. in agricultural economics and marketing from the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign.
notes: Strong energy angle: Gavilon had an energy arm, and Bunge is a big renewable diesel and SAF feedstock supplier. He speaks often at ag industry events such as the NGFA convention in 2026.

name: Christopher Swift
current_role: Chairman & CEO, The Hartford (HIG); becomes Executive Chair on 1 Mar 2027, when Mo Tooker takes over as CEO
profile: CPA who began at KPMG, where he rose to head its Global Insurance Industry Practice, then held senior finance roles at AIG. He joined The Hartford as CFO in 2010, became CEO in 2014 and Chairman in 2015. He refocused it on P&C and group benefits, selling the Japanese annuity business and buying Aetna's group life/disability unit and Navigators. Succession to Mo Tooker was announced in Sept 2026.
interesting_fact: During his tenure The Hartford returned about $22bn to shareholders (2010-June 2026) and nearly doubled P&C written premium to $18bn in 2025. In 2017 it also helped pledge $50m to the City of Hartford.
deep_cut_fact: In a 2015 interview he summed up the business: 'An insurance company sells a promise.' He has also championed The Hartford's Junior Fire Marshal programme, created in 1947, whose red helmets have reached over 110 million children.
notes: Marquette University accounting graduate and trustee (2017-). He is in transition: Executive Chair from March 2027 and plans to leave in H2 2027, so he may have more time for a podcast in 2027.

name: Brian P. Golson
current_role: Managing Partner & Co-CEO, Parthenon Capital; director (Parthenon designee), loanDepot (LDI)
profile: Private-equity investor who has been a co-leader of Parthenon Capital since 2002. Parthenon is a growth-oriented PE firm focused on financial services, tech and healthcare services, and is a large early backer of mortgage lender loanDepot. He sits on loanDepot's board as a Parthenon designee and on portfolio boards such as Payroc, DaySmart and KBRA. His wealth comes largely from PE carry and loanDepot shares.
interesting_fact: Parthenon backed loanDepot early, around 2009-10, when it was a young online mortgage lender. Golson has been on its board since, and loanDepot later became one of the largest US non-bank lenders.
deep_cut_fact: Before private equity he was CFO and VP of Operations at Everdream, a dot-com-era managed desktop services startup. He started his career at GE Capital and holds a UNC-Chapel Hill BA (1992) and a Harvard MBA (1997).
notes: Low public profile. The bio details come from aggregators (KANDO/Mergr) because Parthenon's site blocked automated access, so verify before using the deep cut. Sources place him in Austin, TX, or heading the San Francisco office. The best route is likely through Parthenon Capital.
